title: I Took the Gym Chalk Policy Straight to the Front Desk Camera

parts.text: I clapped chalk off my hands and watched the manager write me up. I am thirty-five, not a manager here, just a member with a 5 a.m. badge. The new rule banned loose chalk. Liquid only, $18 a bottle from the desk. I had a $4 block from the climbing shop, same magnesium. The desk guy, Cody, smelled like energy drinks. The squat rack still had last night's sweat on the knurling. A trainer named Vee whispered that Cody gets a spiff on bottles. Cody said, "That's a write-up for unauthorized powder" I said, "Your sheet says it starts tomorrow" I photographed the rule sheet, dated tomorrow. They were enforcing it a day early on people they disliked. I am unlikeable at 5 a.m. I am also correct. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. parts.text: I asked the camera to see the date with me. Cody laughed, then stopped when I requested the manager, Alina, via the app. Alina arrived with coffee that smelled burnt in a comforting way. She read the sheet. Tomorrow. She voided the write-up. I still bought liquid chalk once, later, on a travel day. Cody lost the spiff program after three other members forwarded photos. Vee got a better slot on the schedule. I keep the $4 block in a baggie. The knurling is still sweaty at 5 a.m. That is a gym. I did not need a write-up to prove it. Alina said, "Why is this dated tomorrow" Cody said, "I thought we were starting early" Alina posted the real start date on the door. Cody says hi now like we share a joke. We share a timestamp.
